pr_body:
This PR fixes #6198 

Things like `IMPORT` are pragmas that resolve to a query with multiple statements.
When this is passed to `Prepare` directly this throws an error.

Instead of providing this directly to Prepare we now first use ExtractStatements to get the statements, if there are more than one we directly execute everything but the last one.

issue_context.title: Nodejs client: Import fails with "Cannot prepare multiple statements"
comments: Can you provide the resulting `load.sql` and `schema.sql` files produced at `EXPORT`?

are there any other files in that folder?
`test_.csv` and `test.csv` should be the only other ones
(Though I think those also shouldn't be present, as we did not populate the table at all)

@Tishj - yeah, there are two files (attached) [test_.csv](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/files/10712956/test_.csv) [test.csv](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/files/10712957/test.csv) These are the only two additional files in the folder:

I'm looking into this now, and this error is thrown when ClientContext::Prepare is called with a string containing multiple queries.

I'm still not sure how that happens here, as your example looks correct

Ah the bug is starting to make sense (but it is definitely a bug)

In Prepare we call ParseStatementsInternal, which resolves pragmas
`import` is a pragma, and resolves to an amalgamation of all the queries contained in the folder.

And as stated above, Prepare throws an error when the query to prepare contains multiple statements, which it does.
```
(lldb) p statements[2]->ToString()
(std::string) $2 = "COPY test FROM './tmp/test.csv' ( FORMAT csv, delimiter \",\", header 0, quote \"\"\"\", compression zstd )"
(lldb) p statements[3]->ToString()
(std::string) $3 = "COPY test2 FROM './tmp/test_.csv' ( FORMAT csv, delimiter \",\", header 0, quote \"\"\"\", compression zstd )"
```

Likely we should change the `Statement` class in `duckdb_node.hpp` from containing a single `unique_ptr<PreparedStatement>` into a vector of them, and then call ExtractStatements, Prepare'ing them separately afterwards.

Just not sure how this change propagates throughout the rest of the Statement handling code

review_comments: Can we wrap the entire function into one big try/catch block? `PendingQuery` is not covered by the try/catch and there's a bunch of duplicate exception handling logic.
